answer: A stake bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before transacting, and reputation accrues only from verified honest work. An attacker spawning thousands of fake identities must fund each one, so the cost scales with every new island of sockpuppets while an honest agent pays once. A pigment-style behavioral fingerprint hashes each agent's interaction pattern, letting the network spot clusters of copies sharing one signature. Random saffron-grade audits then sample agents for checks, so a flood of fakes risks losing deposits across the whole cluster.
